title: Design System: Ubeyd Gencer — Referans Kılavuzu

h-yellow.purpose: Section 1 board. The one hue that takes dark ink — white on it is 2.08:1.

h-orange.purpose: Section 2 board and the Acsa Otomotiv subsection tone.

h-grass.purpose: Subsection tone only: group head plus the index row's reveal bar.

h-vermilion.purpose: Held out of the wheel. Appears in .errata alone, as an 8% wash, a 55% border and a solid 0.34rem square.

leaf.purpose: The reading field, composited over the board at a runtime-solved alpha (0.7209 yellow / 0.8687 orange / 0.8743 teal in light theme).

leaf-dark.purpose: The dark-theme leaf. Solved alpha 0.7307 yellow / 0.4063 orange / 0.3142 teal over the board dimmed to 38%.

ink.purpose: Body text, headings, entry names. ~13.7:1 on every light-theme reading field.

ink-dark.purpose: Dark-theme primary type. 12.8-13.3:1 on the dark reading field.

ink-2.purpose: The machine voice: refs, spec tags, state labels, captions, folio. ~6.0:1 in light.

ink-2-dark.purpose: Dark-theme secondary. 5.7-5.9:1 on the dark reading field.

rule.purpose: Repeating separators inside a list or table, and the specimen-plate border.

rule-strong.purpose: A boundary that closes a region: folio, colophon, panel, lever, jump underline.

display.purpose: One per page: the cover word. Archivo compressed at wdth 76 / wght 800, uppercase, balanced wrap.

display-sm.purpose: The same face at section-title scale for pages 2 and 3.

headline.purpose: Index entry names. Sentence case — these are proper nouns.

title.purpose: Tracked caps hanging in the margin column, with a mono sub-line for reference number and count.

body.purpose: EB Garamond 17/26 against the 62ch measure. Every reading paragraph.

lede.purpose: The opening passage of a section, one step up from body.

label.purpose: Azeret Mono. Codes, refs, versions, domains, measurements, tabular data, controls. Never a spoken sentence.

label-sm.purpose: Spec tags, state labels, errata slips, lever buttons, section sub-lines, table row heads.

spine.purpose: Vertical binding text: name, manual title, version. Coloured by mixing board into ink, never by opacity.

shadows.name: leaf
shadows.purpose: The reading field over the board, light theme. Soft on all four sides — a hard block shadow is not this world's material.

shadows.name: leaf-dark
shadows.purpose: The same object in dark theme: deeper cast, light hairline instead of dark.

shadows.name: punch
shadows.purpose: Binding hole and live-state mark, over color-mix(in srgb, var(--board-face) 62%, #000 38%). One formula, shared exactly.

shadows.name: window-hole
shadows.purpose: The smaller holes punched into a .window, over 60% board / 40% black.

shadows.name: tab-dimple
shadows.purpose: The hole punched in the current tab, over var(--board-face).

motion.name: step
motion.purpose: The only duration in the system. Collapses to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: hinge
motion.purpose: The only timing function. Two frames, no interpolation — a binder hinge does not ease. No cubic-bezier belongs in this codebase.

breakpoints.name: four-column
breakpoints.purpose: Sheet at four content columns; the .fold grid places the particulars panel in the right column.

breakpoints.name: two-column
breakpoints.purpose: Sheet collapses to two columns, margin narrows to 7rem, panel moves under the bio, index rows drop to two columns.

breakpoints.name: one-column
breakpoints.purpose: Sheet collapses to one column, heads move above content, rail fixes at 3rem (44.8px target after the tab offset), TOC leader is dropped.

breakpoints.name: table-block
breakpoints.purpose: The specification table breaks to block layout, row head above row value.

leafSolver.where: Inline <script> in every page's <head>, before first paint; re-run by manual.js via window.solveLeaf() on every theme change.
leafSolver.method: Binary search over sRGB source-over compositing of the acetate leaf on the board hue, targeting a fixed relative luminance for the reading field.

constants.reachabilityPad: (max - min) * 0.08 on the two endpoint luminances

clamps.target: Squeezes the requested luminance into [min+pad, max-pad] of the reachable range. Without it an out-of-range target solves to alpha 0 and the dark leaf vanishes entirely. Never fires on the three shipped hues — it is a guard for hues added later.
clamps.alpha: Keeps the sheet a sheet: below 0.2 the acetate stops reading as a material, above 0.97 it stops reading as acetate.

notes: Each page hardcodes its own hue key (H['yellow'] / H['orange'] / H['teal']); the solver does not read data-board. Adding a board means editing every page head.
In dark theme the solver also writes the dimmed board back as an inline --board-face; in light it removes that inline property and lets the html[data-board] rule stand.
The CSS fallbacks --leaf-a: 0.92 (light) / 0.86 (dark) are a no-JS legibility floor, not design values.
Aligned 2026-08-18: CSS --leaf-rgb now declares 20 18 16, matching the head solver's dark leaf source exactly, so alpha is solved against the colour that is actually painted.

fonts.note: Subset to the site's actual character set with the variation axes preserved. font-display: swap on all three. No third-party font request.

components.name: Binding Edge
components.description: The left edge of every page: two punched holes and a vertical spine imprint carrying name, manual title and version. Fixed, aria-hidden, pointer-events none.
components.html: UBEYD GENCER · REFERANS KILAVUZU · SÜRÜM 2026.08

narrative.overview:
This is a boxed-software reference manual rendered in a browser. The page ground is a divider board printed at full saturation — no tints, no mixing — and a milk-acetate leaf floats on it carrying every word of the reading field. The board is never decoration: it shows on all four sides of the leaf, so the section's hue is a page-scale commitment rather than an accent. The left edge is a real binding: two punched holes and a vertical spine imprint carrying the name, the manual title and the version. The right edge is the fore edge, where a stepped tab rail gives one tab per section, each tab's height proportional to that section's extent.

The two themes are the same object under different light. Light is acetate over board under room light. Dark is the identical board dimmed to 38% under a smoked acetate — the hue survives, the illumination does not. Nothing about the layout, the grid, the tab proportions or the type changes between them; only the light does.

The system refuses easing. Every transition in the stylesheet is var(--step) var(--hinge) — 90ms at steps(2, end), two frames, no interpolation. A binder hinge does not ease. This is a deliberate override of ordinary ease-out guidance and it is the motion grammar of the whole world; a cubic-bezier anywhere in this codebase is a foreign body. Depth is likewise material, not effect: one soft offset shadow under the leaf, one edge-light gradient along its fore edge, inset shadows in the punched holes. Nothing glows, nothing lifts on hover.
keyCharacteristics: Full-saturation board hue as page ground, visible on all four sides of the leaf
Runtime-solved leaf alpha holding a fixed reading luminance on every board hue, in both themes
Real binding furniture: punched holes, vertical spine imprint, stepped fore-edge tab rail
No easing anywhere — 90ms steps(2, end) on every transition
Three self-hosted variable faces (Archivo / EB Garamond / Azeret Mono), 136 KB total
Every state carries a word as well as a mark; colour is never the sole signal
Foreign imagery enters only through punched windows and bordered specimen plates

rules.name: The Errata Reserve Rule
rules.body: Vermilion (#C42208) appears in .errata and nowhere else. If a new surface needs a warning colour, it does not get one — it gets an errata slip or it gets words.

rules.name: The Literal Dark Ink Rule
rules.body: --on-tone for .t-yellow is the literal #17150F, never var(--ink). White on chrome yellow measures 2.08:1; --ink flips with the theme but a subsection tone does not (it is only filtered), so var(--ink) would put light text on yellow in dark theme. The sibling --on-board for html[data-board="yellow"] is var(--ink), and correctly so: the board itself dims with the theme, so the ink must flip with it.

rules.name: The Solved Leaf Rule
rules.body: Never hand-pick --leaf-a. Adding a board hue means adding it to the solver's H table and letting the bisection answer; a literal alpha that looks right on one hue is wrong on the next.

rules.name: The Full-Saturation Rule
rules.body: Board hues ship at their printed values. They are not tinted, shaded or mixed with each other. The only sanctioned modulations are the solver's uniform 0.38 dim in dark theme and the documented color-mix recipes (punch holes at 62% board / 38% black, window ground at 12% board, panel ground at 6% board).

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono is confined to machine content: codes, reference numbers, versions, domains, measurements, tabular data, state labels, UI controls. A sentence a person would say out loud is never set in mono, and a code is never set in Garamond.

rules.name: The Turkish Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Under lang="tr", text-transform: uppercase maps ASCII i to İ — logitech.com becomes LOGİTECH.COM. Domains are therefore never uppercased: .toc__val and .jump deliberately omit text-transform while every other mono register carries it. ASCII technology names inside Turkish pages are tagged lang="en" on the element so casing and hyphenation resolve in English.

rules.name: The Hanging Head Rule
rules.body: Section heads live in the margin column, not above the content. They are set in tracked caps at 0.75rem and hang left of the reading field; only below 1180px does the margin narrow, and only below 760px does the head drop above its content with a rule under it.

rules.name: The Four Margins Rule
rules.body: The board is visible on all four sides of the leaf at every width. Never let the leaf bleed to an edge; the tone is the page-scale commitment and a leaf that touches the viewport edge destroys it.

rules.name: The Fore-Edge Rule
rules.body: The tab rail stays on the fore edge at every width — it is the manual's identity. Under pressure the leaf narrows; the rail does not become a hamburger, a top bar, or a drawer.

rules.name: The Proportional Tab Rule
rules.body: Tab height is content extent, not label length. .rail li consumes flex: var(--extent, 1) 1 0 and every <li> writes its own --extent inline (currently 1 / 3.1 / 2.4 for Introduction / Projects / Bookmarks). Add a section and you must give it an extent, or the rail silently falls back to equal thirds.

rules.name: The No-Easing Rule
rules.body: Every transition in this system is var(--step) var(--hinge) — 90ms, steps(2, end). No cubic-bezier, no ease-out, no spring, anywhere. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, --step becomes 1ms and animations are forced to 1ms / 1 iteration.

rules.name: The Four Properties Rule
rules.body: Only four properties are ever transitioned in this build: translate (tab pull), filter (dark tab dimming), opacity (the entry reveal bar), background/color (lever and control buttons), and border-color (jump underline). Nothing transitions size, position or shadow. Filtering the projects list re-deals rows with hidden — a hinge step, never a fade.

rules.name: The Punch-Not-Glow Rule
rules.body: A recess is an inset shadow over a darkened board mix. A live state is a hole, not an LED. Painting the live mark at full board value broke this once — it stopped matching the site's own punch grammar and read as a light source in dark theme.

rules.name: The Punched Window Rule
rules.body: Foreign imagery enters only through a punched window. .window is the plate (.window--plate caps the image at 30rem); .window--thumb is the contact-print scale used in index rows, with the holes and padding tightened and an 8:5 top-anchored crop. Bookmark favicons sit on .mark, a bordered specimen plate on an opaque leaf ground. An never floats free on the leaf.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is 1px hairlines, not fills and not shadows. --rule for repeating separators inside a list or table, --rule-strong for a boundary that closes a region (folio, colophon, panel, lever).

rules.name: The One Lever Rule
rules.body: A single control re-deals the whole field. Pressing a lever button hides non-matching .entry rows, closes any group whose visible count reaches zero together with its margin-column head, and updates both the per-group count and the page tally in the same move. There is no per-group filter and no multi-select.

rules.name: The Word-And-Mark Rule
rules.body: Every state carries a word as well as a mark. The mark is aria-hidden; the word is the accessible name. Colour and shape are never the sole signal.

dos: Do add a board hue by adding it to the solver's H table in every page's <head> and to the html[data-board] rule with an --on-board value, then let the bisection publish --leaf-a.
Do give every new rail section an inline --extent proportional to its content; without it the tab silently falls back to flex: 1.
Do write var(--step) var(--hinge) for every transition — 90ms, steps(2, end).
Do confine Azeret Mono to machine content: codes, refs, versions, domains, measurements, tabular data, state labels, controls.
Do set body copy in EB Garamond at 17/26 against the 62ch --measure.
Do tag ASCII technology names inside Turkish pages with lang="en".
Do pair every state mark with its word, and mark the glyph aria-hidden="true".
Do frame any foreign image in a .window or a .mark specimen plate.
Do use color-mix(in srgb, var(--board-face) …) when a surface needs to acknowledge the section tone — 62%/38% black for a punch, 12% for a window ground, 6% for a panel.
Do keep the board visible on all four sides of the leaf at every width.
donts: Don't write --on-tone: var(--ink) for .t-yellow. It must be the literal #17150F; tones do not flip with the theme, and white on chrome yellow is 2.08:1.
Don't hand-pick --leaf-a. The CSS fallbacks (0.92 / 0.86) are a no-JS floor, not design values.
Don't introduce an easing curve, a spring, a fade, or a duration other than --step. No cubic-bezier belongs in this codebase.
Don't uppercase a domain. Under lang="tr", text-transform: uppercase turns ASCII i into İ.
Don't put a hard offset block shadow on the leaf or any other surface; this world's shadow is soft and singular.
Don't paint the current tab in the board colour — it lands on the ground's exact pixel value and the current section loses its sign. Paint it in the leaf.
Don't paint the live-state mark at full board value; use the binding punch's 62%/38% formula so it reads as a hole rather than an LED.
Don't collapse the rail into a hamburger, top bar, or drawer at any width.
Don't add filled chips, badges, pills, or cards. Credits are bottom-ruled captions and containers are hairline boxes.
Don't let a circle mean anything but a punched hole.
Don't signal state with colour alone.
